problem_text:
A network of six remote research stations requires a maintenance team to conduct a periodic inspection circuit. The stations are positioned at the following GPS waypoints:

Station Alpha: (41,87)
Station Bravo: (135,64)
Station Charlie: (30,152)
Station Delta: (113,170)
Station Echo: (44,3)
Station Foxtrot: (120,174)

Travel distances between stations, measured in nautical miles, are predefined:

Alpha to Charlie: 65.9 nm
Alpha to Delta: 109.9 nm
Alpha to Echo: 84.1 nm
Alpha to Foxtrot: 117.5 nm
Bravo to Charlie: 137.0 nm
Bravo to Delta: 108.3 nm
Bravo to Echo: 109.6 nm
Bravo to Foxtrot: 111.0 nm
Charlie to Delta: 84.9 nm
Charlie to Echo: 149.7 nm
Charlie to Foxtrot: 92.6 nm
Delta to Echo: 180.7 nm
Delta to Foxtrot: 8.1 nm
Echo to Foxtrot: 187.1 nm

Due to permanent terrain obstructions, direct transit between Station Alpha and Station Bravo is impossible. Furthermore, operational protocol mandates that the inspection route must incorporate exactly one of two critical supply corridors: either the link between Station Bravo and Station Charlie, or the link between Station Charlie and Station Delta.

The objective is to determine the most efficient closed-loop itinerary that visits every station precisely once and returns to the point of origin, minimizing the total distance traversed.
